D007-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been like this for about seven months now. It started with feeling…blank. I used to love my work at the library—curating collections, running reading groups—but now even when we win grants or get compliments from the board, it’s like it happens to someone else. I just don’t care. I move through the days on autopilot, exhausted even after a full night’s sleep, and still I pace my flat half the night, picking at my cuticles, unable to sit still.

About six months ago, the other things began. I started to notice my…friend, the man I’ve been seeing, pulling away. I’m certain he’s seeing someone else, even though I’ve never caught him, never found messages. The conviction is just there, like a fact, and it eats at me. Sometimes, even when my mood is more or less steady, I still see people standing between the shelves after closing—figures that vanish when I walk toward them. That’s gone on for weeks at a time, separate from the worst of the gloom.

At work, when people ask simple questions, my answers wander off; I’ll start talking about cataloguing and end up on some tangent about old manuscripts, never really answering. It’s become hard to function as the person I used to be.
D007-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling low for about seven months now, pretty much every day. It’s like this heavy cloud that doesn’t lift. I move slower; even mopping the hallway at the building takes me twice as long because my body just feels weighed down. My wife says I shuffle around the apartment. I don’t really talk to the tenants like I used to, and I’ve been avoiding family gatherings, just sitting in the back room by myself.

Nights are bad. I lie in bed for hours, staring at the ceiling, unable to fall asleep even though I’m exhausted. While I’m lying there, I get this absolute certainty that everything is going to end soon, that the whole world is about to collapse, like there’s no point in fixing a leaky pipe because nothing will be left anyway. That’s been going on for about six months.

Sometimes I feel things crawling under my skin, like tiny bugs running up my arms, but when I look there’s nothing there. I’ll mutter to myself using what my wife calls my “jumble words” — like “gloomfog” and “skin-sparks” — they make sense to me, but no one else understands. These strange thoughts and sensations have carried on even during a couple of weeks when, oddly, my mood wasn’t quite as dark, though most of the time the sadness and the odd experiences are happening together.
D007-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h003.question:
For about seven months now I’ve felt like I’ve just…gone flat. I used to love sketching buildings for fun after work; now I don’t get any pleasure from it, or from anything really. Most days I wake up feeling heavy and miserable, even if I’ve technically slept 8–9 hours. It’s like the sleep doesn’t “take,” and I get out of bed already exhausted. My colleagues comment that I’m quieter; even answering basic questions in meetings, I notice I pause a long time, searching for words, and my speech feels slowed down.

Around six months ago, on top of that, I became convinced that a client—someone fairly high‑profile—is secretly in love with me. I “see signs” in her emails and project comments that she’s sending me messages. Part of me knows it doesn’t quite add up, but it still feels true. I also keep smelling cigarette smoke and something like burning plastic in my apartment and office when no one else notices anything.

These beliefs and smells were there for a couple of weeks before I really crashed mood‑wise, and they’ve stayed with me throughout, but the low mood and loss of interest have been the main thing most of this time. It’s gotten hard to keep up with deadlines and I’ve turned down new projects because I just can’t function like I used to. Sometimes when I’m really tired my thoughts drift into wordplay — like “plans, spans, fans” — and I’ll catch myself stringing rhymes instead of saying what I actually mean.
D007-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h004.question:
I guess this started about seven months ago. I’m crying all the time now, even at work. I’ll be in the back placing an IV on a cat and just feel tears running down my face for no real reason. I used to love my job and fostering dogs, but lately I just… don’t care. I go straight home, lie on the couch, ignore my friends’ texts.

My sleep is awful. I fall asleep okay, but then I’m up two, three times a night, staring at the ceiling for hours. I get so restless I end up pacing around my apartment at 3 a.m., or picking at the skin on my arms until it’s raw. I can’t sit still but I’m exhausted.

For the last six months I’ve also been convinced something is wrong inside my body. I’m sure my organs are rotting, like they’re decaying. I can actually smell this sickly, sweet, rotten-meat smell that no one else seems to notice, even in the clinic. There was a couple of weeks early on where it was just that—those smells and this belief my body was falling apart—without me feeling as low, but since then the sadness and hopelessness have pretty much been there the whole time. It’s getting really hard to function at work.
D007-D005_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h005.question:
It’s been about seven months now that I’ve felt…flat and heavy all the time. I wake up already tired, and most days I end up sleeping 12, 14 hours if I don’t set alarms. Even then, I just lie there because moving feels like walking through mud. I used to love shooting content, planning outfits, talking to my followers, but now nothing feels enjoyable. I just don’t care, even when brand deals come in. It’s like everything’s dulled out.

Around six months ago, on top of that, things started getting strange. I’m convinced this one super‑famous musician is secretly in love with me. I can see “signs” in his posts and interviews, like he’s sending me messages. Sometimes I even see him, or other people, standing in my room or at the end of my bed, but when I look again they’re gone. When I talk about it I catch myself jumping from my DMs to my neighbor’s dog to the meaning of colors, and I lose track of what I was saying.

There were a couple of weeks where the sadness lifted a bit, but the visions and the feeling that he loves me still stayed. Overall, though, this low mood and lack of interest have been there pretty much the whole time and have really wrecked my ability to work.
D007-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h006.question:
It’s been about a year and a half now that I’ve felt…hollow, I guess. Not sad exactly, more like there’s nothing inside. Things I used to love—designing planting plans, walking sites, even just sitting in the garden with my husband—feel flat. I don’t get any joy out of them. My appetite’s dropped off too; most days I have to force myself to eat.

Alongside that, for about a year and four months, I’ve been convinced something terrible is coming. It feels certain, like the world is collapsing in slow motion, and I’m somehow to blame. I’ll hear about a flood on the news and “know” it happened because I didn’t speak up about climate change enough in my projects. I understand that doesn’t really make sense, but it feels absolutely true.

Sometimes, out of nowhere, my mouth fills with this chemical, almost metallic taste, like fertilizer or pesticide, even when I’m just drinking water. When I try to explain what’s going on, my thoughts jump around—I’ll start talking about a planting plan and suddenly I’m on disasters and then my childhood, and I lose track of what I was saying.

Even during a couple of weeks when my mood wasn’t as low, the certainty that everything was ending and that strange taste didn’t go away. This whole time, the emptiness and loss of interest have been there more days than not, and it’s gotten hard to keep up with work and even basic things at home.
D007-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year and a half now. It started with this deep, hollow feeling, like I’m just…blank inside. I used to be very engaged at work—home visits, court reports, talking with families—but now I mostly shut my office door and avoid my coworkers. Even at home, my husband says I’ve “disappeared” into myself. I don’t really feel much of anything, just this heavy emptiness. I’ve lost over 20 pounds in a month or so without trying—food just doesn’t interest me.

Around the same time, I started becoming convinced that my agency and the families I work with are monitoring me, like there’s some system tracking everything I do. I “see” people standing in corners or at the end of the hallway, staring at me, but when I look properly, they’re gone. It’s scary, but also feels weirdly normal now.

I can’t shake the belief that I’m responsible for bad outcomes in cases I never even worked on—kids getting hurt, families breaking down—like it’s all somehow my fault. This low, empty state and the guilt have been there most of the time, even when the visions and the feeling of being watched briefly eased up for a couple of weeks. When I try to explain all this, I start talking about work policies or old cases and lose track of what you actually asked.
D007-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h008.question:
It started about a year and a half ago. First I just felt…blank. I used to love being on the floor at the restaurant, talking to customers, tweaking recipes. Now I walk in and feel nothing. It’s like I’m hollowed out. I stay in the office more, staring at the cameras, not even tasting the food. I’ve gained a lot of weight this past year because I just sit in the back and pick at whatever’s around instead of actually enjoying a proper meal.

Most days I don’t want to do anything, but at the same time I’m convinced I’ve somehow ruined people’s lives. If a supplier’s truck crashes on the highway, I’m sure it’s because of something I did, or some thought I had. I can’t shake the idea that small things—like a couple at table 4 whispering—are actually about me, criticizing me. Even the radio in the kitchen feels like it’s sending me messages.

Sometimes, especially late at night doing inventory, I feel things crawling on my arms or my back, like bugs, but there’s nothing there. When I talk to my husband, I start on one thing and suddenly I’m off on something completely different, and he looks confused. This emptiness and all these thoughts have been there almost the whole time this has been going on, though there were a couple of weeks when the strange beliefs and the skin sensations kept going even when my mood felt more “neutral.” It’s gotten hard to keep the restaurant running and to be present at home.
D007-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h009.question:
It started about a year and a half ago with this heavy, flat feeling. I used to love planning campaigns and scrolling for fun, but now I mostly just schedule posts and log off. Even when a campaign does really well, I feel…nothing. It’s like my emotions are on mute. I’ve put on a lot of weight in a short time because I just sit and snack all day; I don’t really care what I look like anymore.

For most of this time I’ve also been convinced people are watching me. Not just followers—like companies, maybe even the government, tracking me through my phone and laptop. At home, I sometimes feel something crawling on my skin or like someone’s lightly touching my arm, but there’s nothing there. When I talk about it, I catch myself jumping from my job to my neighbor’s dog to some random conspiracy and then forgetting what I was even saying.

I’m sure it’s my fault when bad things happen—celebrity deaths, accidents I see online—like I somehow caused them by posting the wrong thing. Even during a short stretch a few months ago when the sadness lifted a bit, the feeling of being monitored and those skin sensations never really went away. This has all really messed with my work and my social life.
D007-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h010.question:
I guess it started about a year and a half ago, maybe a bit more. At first it was just feeling…hollow. Like someone scooped everything out of me. I still turn in my webtoon every week, but it’s more out of autopilot than caring. Readers comment nice things, my editor says the numbers are good, but it barely registers. It’s like, “So what?” I used to obsess over panels and storylines; now I just eat and draw. I’ve been eating a lot more, especially late at night, and I’ve actually put on weight, but I can’t bring myself to care either way.

Most days, I wake up thinking I’m useless, that my work and I don’t really matter. That feeling’s been there nearly every day for over a year, and it’s made everything harder—deadlines, meeting friends, even showering.

Around a year and a few months ago, other things started. I keep thinking random stuff online, like fan comments or tweets, are secretly about me, like they’re coded messages. Sometimes I smell smoke or something rotten in my room when there’s nothing there. When people ask what’s wrong, I try to explain, but my thoughts wander off and I end up talking about something else entirely.

There were a couple of weeks when the weird smells and feeling watched by messages were really intense, even though my mood wasn’t especially low—just kind of flat. But most of the time, the emptiness and worthlessness have been there alongside the strange beliefs and smells, and the low mood has really been the main thing weighing me down.
D007-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been working offshore on the rigs for years, but about seven months ago everything went off the rails. Around the same time I started hearing these voices almost every day, like people talking just over my shoulder, saying the world’s about to end, that everything is going to be wiped out. It’s not just a feeling—I'm convinced some huge disaster is coming, like there’s no point to anything because it’s all going to be destroyed.

Most days I feel completely empty. Things I used to like—cards with the guys, calling my family on shore leave—now I just don’t care. I mostly keep to myself; I avoid the others on the platform. I pace up and down the corridor or wring my hands without even realizing it, or pick at the skin on my fingers until they bleed. I can’t sit still, but I also don’t enjoy anything.

Sometimes when I talk, I lose track and the words come out all jumbled, like my mouth is moving faster than my thoughts. I catch myself doing these odd little repeated movements with my hands when I walk. I keep thinking everything bad that happens on the rig is my fault, like if a tool breaks it’s because I’m a terrible person and deserve to be punished. I think about dying a lot—“it’d be better if I just wasn’t here”—but I haven’t made a plan. This has been going on pretty much nonstop these whole seven months, apart from a couple of weeks when the sadness dipped but the voices and end-of-the-world stuff kept going. I’m barely managing to work now; the supervisor’s already cut my shifts.
D007-D005_h011.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h012.question:
It started about seven months ago. At first I just felt…flat. I used to love showing homes, chatting people up, closing deals. Now I don’t get any joy from it, or from anything really—not my kids, not my husband, not even our date nights. I move like I’m walking through mud; my coworkers comment that I’m “slowing down,” shuffling around the office, taking forever to grab files or get out of the car. I barely talk in meetings anymore—just short answers, if any.

Most days I feel completely useless, like my family would be better off without me. I’ve even picked out a bridge on my drive route and thought through when I’d go there and what I’d bring so I wouldn’t be stopped.

On top of that, I’m convinced something terrible is coming, like the world is about to collapse and nothing we do matters. Sometimes I smell this strong burning or rotten odor when no one else does. My husband says I sit on the couch rocking my hands or tapping my fingers over and over without realizing it. When things get really bad, my thoughts jumble and what comes out of my mouth is just a mess of words, even I can’t follow it.  

The low mood and emptiness have been there almost this whole time, but there were a couple of weeks when I mostly just had the strange smells and the sense the world was ending, without feeling as down.
D007-D005_h012.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h013.question:
For about seven months now, it feels like everything has come apart at the same time. I’m working from home on articles, but I move so slowly it’s almost painful—just walking to the kitchen or typing an email feels like wading through mud. I used to care about getting pitches accepted, building my portfolio; now, even when something gets published, I just feel…nothing. It doesn’t matter. I don’t matter. Most days I’m convinced I’m a waste of space.

Around the same time this started, I became convinced something is seriously wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting or rearranging themselves. No tests show anything, but I can’t shake it. I also feel things crawling or brushing on my skin, like insects or fingers, when there’s nothing there. Sometimes I catch myself tapping the table in the same pattern for minutes, or rocking in my chair without realizing it.

My speech gets weird too—I’ll start rhyming or stringing together words just because they sound alike. I’ve pulled away from friends and my ex; I barely answer texts. The low mood has been there almost the whole time, but there were a couple of weeks when the strange body beliefs and skin sensations kept going even though I didn’t feel especially sad—just empty and detached. D007-D005_h014.question:
It started about seven months ago. I’m a patrol sergeant, so I’m used to being in control, but lately I keep thinking I’m…more than human. I catch myself believing I’ve got this special mission, like I can sense danger before it happens, like I’m some kind of chosen protector. It feels completely real when I’m on the street.

I hear voices pretty much every day now, even when I’m alone in the squad car. They call my name, tell me I’m destined for “greater power,” then sometimes tell me I’m useless. No radio, no one around, but I still hear them.

My wife says I just sit there with a blank face. I barely look at her or the kids. Talking feels like pushing through mud—I need a few seconds before I can answer simple questions. I’ve pulled back from everyone at the station, stopped going out with the guys. Most days I feel like I’m a failure as a cop and a father, like there’s no point to me being here. I often think it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans.

There were a couple weeks where the voices and those “chosen” ideas were strong, but my mood wasn’t as low. But overall, these heavy, worthless feelings have been hanging over almost this entire time.
D007-D005_h014.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h015.question:

I’ve been very down most of this time—like a heavy weight I can’t shake. I’ve stopped caring about the things I used to enjoy, like watching football or doing little projects around the house. I’ve thought a lot about ending my life—imagining hanging myself in the garage late at night when everyone’s asleep, planning how I’d do it. Even on the few days when my mood dips slightly less, the beliefs about that woman and the figures I see in the hallway have stayed with me for at least a couple of weeks at a time. D007-D005_h015.options:

    D. Schizophrenia
